headline: A private key created by any WebCrypto implementation now signs and exports across the toolkit -- a key from the platform's own WebCrypto previously reached the crypto library as a key it could not read, and failed with a type error instead of a reason.
summary: This toolkit ships its own WebCrypto engine, and a CryptoKey it created is indistinguishable from one the platform created by type, algorithm and usages -- but the two hold their key material in different places, and neither can export the other's. A caller holding a key from the platform's WebCrypto, or from a browser, followed the documented "pass a CryptoKey" contract and got a type error raised from inside the crypto library naming an internal property. Every documented entry point now accepts a key from either: the key is exported through the implementation that owns it and re-imported here, and the signature it produces verifies under the key's own public half, so the material carried across is the same material. A key created non-extractable is reachable by neither implementation; that is a permanent verdict, and it is now refused as itself rather than as a wrong-typed argument. The engine's own keys are unaffected -- one created non-extractable still signs, because it is never exported. The raw WebCrypto surface, where cross-implementation use is left undefined by the specification, refuses such a key with a typed fault naming which implementation it came from.

Fixed: Certificate, CRL, CSR, CMS, attribute-certificate, OCSP, CMP and CRMF signing, together with pki.key.export and pki.jose.sign, accept a private key created by any WebCrypto implementation -- the platform's, a browser's, or this toolkit's. Previously only a key this toolkit itself created would work; any other reached the crypto library as a key with no material behind it and failed with a type error naming an internal property, giving a caller who had followed the documented contract nothing to act on. Signing, private-key export, public-key export and secret-key signing are all covered, across EC, Edwards and RSA keys.

A key created non-extractable can be read by no implementation but the one that made it, so a foreign one cannot be reached at all. That is now refused with that as the reason, and with the two ways forward -- import it through this toolkit's WebCrypto, or pass the key as DER -- rather than being reported as an argument of the wrong type. A non-extractable key this toolkit created is unaffected and still signs, since it is used in place rather than exported.

pki.webcrypto.subtle refuses a key created by a different WebCrypto implementation with a typed fault that names which implementation it came from, and distinguishes it from an argument that is no key at all. The specification leaves cross-implementation use undefined; every operation that reads key material -- sign, verify, encrypt, decrypt, key derivation and encapsulation, wrapping, and export -- previously let a bare type error escape from inside the crypto library instead. The counterpart public key of a key-agreement operation, which travels in the algorithm rather than as the key argument, is checked on the same footing.
